reuse.why: All occurrence consumers reuse the extended getDateWithSkippedWeekend helper, although configuration gating and occurrence-search policy remain distributed.

duplication.why: Weekend enablement and forwarding of mode, frequency, and holidays are repeated across getNextDate, applyWeekendSkip, and getOccurrenceDay.

placement.why: Working-day rules remain in shared scheduling utilities, with handler registration, rule metadata, and budget aggregation in their existing layers.

scope.why: The changes are focused on the requested scheduling rules, range handler, supporting metadata, and tests.

maintainability.why: The central adjustment helper is understandable, but separate over-fetch and range-margin formulas make consumers responsible for coordinating search policy with evolving scheduling rules.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All changed occurrence-adjustment paths call getDateWithSkippedWeekend.

disguised_duplication.where: The repeated configuration gating is direct; holiday matching and date adjustment are shared rather than disguised copies.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains frequency and holidays parameters and a daily-frequency branch returning null; all changed consumers continue using it.
